newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GE pledges two bln rand boost for S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: GE pledges two bln rand boost for S.Africa.

text.p: General Electric Co of the United States said on Monday it had signed an Industrial and Commercial Cooperation Programme Agreement with South Africa, guaranteeing to generate two billion rand in benefits to the country's economy.

GE, the world's largest company by market capitalisation, said there were several ways for it to fulfil its commitment, ranging from direct investment and purchases of locally produced goods, to technology transfers and specialist human resources development.
The deal is only the second such agreement entered into by GE. In return, the agreement provides for the application of incentives under South Africa's National Industrial Participation Policy.
"GE is committed to doing serious business in South Africa," GE trading company chief executive Stuart Fisher said in a statement.

The company returned to South Africa in 1995 after disinvesting in the 1980s and now has 10 divisions represented in the country -- appliances, aircraft engines, electrical distribution and control, lighting, medical systems, motors and industrial systems, plastics, power systems, silicones and transportation systems.
"We welcome GE committing to the South African economy in such a big way," said Vassie Ponsamy of the Department of Trade and Industry, responsible for industrial participation.
